answer: Kin clustering: the ledger logs when each identity answers, which peers it attests, and how similar its texts are. Identities that move together like a tide, posting within seconds and always vouching for each other, get merged into one cluster that shares a single reward and a single vote. To dodge this, an attacker must give every fake its own schedule, peer set and writing style, which is like carving a mesa out of shale by hand: each extra seat costs nearly as much real work as an honest agent does.
